title: backend: Add Apple iCloud Photos backend
body:
#### What is your current rclone version (output from `rclone version`)?

v1.67

#### What problem are you are trying to solve?

Apple's iCloud can store both files in the iCloud Drive and photos via Apples Photos app.
A new backend for accessing the iCloud Drive is currently beeing finalized in https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/1778 & https://github.com/rclone/rclone/pull/7717

This issues attempts to track the development of extending the initial iCloud Drive support to photos.

#### How do you think rclone should be changed to solve that?

The existing iCloud Drive backend should be extended with support for accessing photos.
@participant6, the author of the initial iCloud backend implementation, has outlined the planned approach [in this comment](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/issues/1778#issuecomment-2029300270):

> > B: single remote includes all available services mapped to their names in the root(so icloudremote:/drive, icloudremote:/photos etc)
> > 
> > C: B but let user choose woch services are avaiable for the remote
> > 
> > A and C are probably quite similar just with a config option to control. One of those sounds the easiest to implement and there is lots of precedent in rclone, eg drive/shared drives or OneDrive/SharePoint
> > 
> 
> im gonna focus on option C. This allows credentials to be defined only once and a user can choose the services from the config.
> 
> **Il write an Fs interface for every service but combine them similar to combine backen to provide a single backend to rclone**

So the plan would be to combine both Drive and Photos in a single backend but use two separate `Fs` implementations internally.

#### How to use GitHub

* Please use the 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to show that you are affected by the same issue.
* Please don't comment if you have no relevant information to add. It's just extra noise for everyone subscribed to this issue.
* Subscribe to receive notifications on status change and new comments.

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
Hey all 👋

I've been working on implementing an iCloud Photos backend for rclone and have made good progress on several key areas:

- Authentication and session handling with iCloud services (leveraging some of @participant6's iclouddrive backend code 🎉)
- Core directory/download functionality working and tested
- Support for both PrimarySync and SharedSync libraries
- Read-only backend implementation following rclone conventions

The implementation is showing promising results across different testing scenarios (120k+ photos), including various album types and media formats.

Next up:

- Continued development and refinement
- Code review and cleanup
- Documentation and testing
- Preparing for community feedback

Happy to discuss the approach or answer any questions about the implementation direction! I'm not really a Go dev, but managing to make some meaningful progress 😄
